name: eng-2350
title: Import shared node type templates into Roam
claim: Importing a node whose type this graph doesn't have creates that node type with the template its source published.
given: test-3-graph has neither type. The Obsidian test vault shared PK Hypothesis, whose template has YAML frontmatter, and one node. The dev graph shared PK Prediction with a template, and one node.

prepare.why: the Obsidian test vault published a PK Hypothesis node type whose template has frontmatter, and one node, to the eng-2329-demo group

types.label: PK Hypothesis
types.template:
---
tags: hypothesis
---
## Prediction
- What should happen if this is true
## How to test it
- The smallest experiment that could fail

nodes.title: Sleep spindles predict recall
nodes.body: Spindle density in the first hour of sleep predicts next-day recall.

prepare.why: the dev graph published a PK Prediction node type with a template, and one node, to the same group

types.label: PK Prediction
types.template:
- Expected result
- How we will know

prepare.why: neither node type nor node was imported into this graph before

check.js: !["discourse-graph/nodes/PK Hypothesis", "discourse-graph/nodes/PK Prediction", "HYP - Sleep spindles predict recall", "[[PRD]] - Recall improves after a nap"].some((title) => proof.page.exists(title))

apply.js: proof.page.remove(["discourse-graph/nodes/PK Hypothesis", "discourse-graph/nodes/PK Prediction", "HYP - Sleep spindles predict recall", "[[PRD]] - Recall improves after a nap"])

prepare.why: the extension has a proof database session for this graph; the proof database runs without edge functions, so this signs in the way create-space would

cases.title: Importing an Obsidian node creates its node type with the template
cases.proves: Done When 2: A new Obsidian-origin node type imports with its template visible in settings.
cases.checks: PK Hypothesis exists, its Template has the Prediction and How to test it sections, and no frontmatter came across
cases.caption: This graph has no Hypothesis type. Importing a hypothesis shared from Obsidian creates the type and brings its template along, without the Obsidian frontmatter.

steps.why: open import the way a user would
wait for the shared node's row

do.click: .bp3-dialog tbody tr:has-text("Sleep spindles predict recall") label.bp3-checkbox

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const lines = proof.nodeType.template('PK Hypothesis'); return lines && lines.some((line) => line.includes('Prediction')) && lines.some((line) => line.includes('smallest experiment')) && !lines.some((line) => /tags:|---/.test(line)); }, { what: "PK Hypothesis's template, without its frontmatter", timeout: 15000 })

cases.title: The new node type's template holds the shared template
cases.checks: the node type's page shows the template text
cases.caption: The new node type carries the template, so new hypotheses in this graph start from it.

steps.why: open the node type's settings page

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => proof.byText('.roam-article', 'smallest experiment'), { what: 'the template on the node type page' })

cases.title: Importing a Roam node creates its node type with the template
cases.proves: Done When 1: A new Roam-origin node type imports with its template visible in settings.
cases.checks: PK Prediction exists with Expected result and How we will know in its Template
cases.caption: It works for node types shared from Roam too. The Prediction type arrives with its template.

do.wait_for: .bp3-dialog tbody tr:has-text("Recall improves after a nap")

steps.why: wait for the shared node's row

do.click: .bp3-dialog tbody tr:has-text("Recall improves after a nap") label.bp3-checkbox

expect.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const lines = proof.nodeType.template('PK Prediction'); return lines && lines.includes('Expected result') && lines.includes('How we will know'); }, { what: "PK Prediction's template", timeout: 15000 })

cases.title: Refreshing imported nodes leaves the templates alone
cases.proves: Done When 3: importing or refreshing again writes nothing
cases.checks: both templates have the same number of blocks as before, and there's one PK Hypothesis type
cases.caption: Refreshing every imported node finds the types already in place, so their templates aren't written twice.

do.js: (() => { window.__pk2350 = { hypothesis: proof.nodeType.template('PK Hypothesis').length, prediction: proof.nodeType.template('PK Prediction').length }; proof.toasts.clear(); })()

steps.why: count the template blocks before the refresh

do.js: proof.waitFor(() => { const text = proof.toastText(); return text && !text.includes('Refreshing imported nodes'); }, { what: 'the refresh to finish', timeout: 30000 })

steps.why: wait for the refresh to finish

expect.js: (() => { const before = window.__pk2350; proof.assert(before, 'No count from before the refresh.'); proof.assert(proof.nodeType.template('PK Hypothesis').length === before.hypothesis, 'The refresh changed the PK Hypothesis template.'); proof.assert(proof.nodeType.template('PK Prediction').length === before.prediction, 'The refresh changed the PK Prediction template.'); proof.assert(proof.nodeTypes().filter((node) => node.text === 'PK Hypothesis').length === 1, 'There is more than one PK Hypothesis node type.'); })()
